# 6. Materials and Methods

## 6.1. Patient Recruitment

## 6.2. Isolation of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) from Whole Blood

Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from freshly collected peripheral venous blood by density gradient centrifugation, adapted from Steffen et al. [@steffenGenerationAnalysisHuman2019]. Blood was collected into heparinised tubes (7.5–35 mL per donor depending on experimental requirements) and the tubes were inverted at least five times immediately after collection to prevent coagulation. Blood was transferred to a 50 mL Falcon tube and diluted 1:1 with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4; Gibco™) at room temperature. SepMate™ tubes (StemCell Technologies) were pre-loaded with 15 mL of RotiSep density medium (Carl Roth) in the lower compartment as per the manufacturer's instructions. The diluted blood was layered gently over the density medium and tubes were centrifuged at 1,200 × g for 10–12 minutes. Centrifuge acceleration and deceleration settings varied across experiments: deceleration 0 was used in initial experiments (July 2023), acceleration 4/deceleration 4 in October 2023, and acceleration 9/deceleration 4 in all subsequent experiments (March 2024 onwards).

Following centrifugation, three distinct layers formed: plasma at the top, a buffy coat enriched for PBMCs at the interface, and a pellet of erythrocytes and granulocytes at the bottom. The plasma layer was decanted and the buffy coat was carefully transferred into a fresh 50 mL Falcon tube. The cell suspension was washed twice with cold PBS (Gibco™, pH 7.4): first at 300 × g for 10–12 minutes (acceleration 9, deceleration 4), followed by a second wash at 200 × g for 10–12 minutes under the same centrifuge settings. The resulting pellet was resuspended in 5 mL adherence medium consisting of α-MEM (Gibco) supplemented with 1% penicillin–streptomycin–glutamine (PSG) and 1% fetal calf serum (FCS, Bio&Sell). <!-- TODO: confirm full FCS (Bio&Sell) lot number — recorded incomplete in lab notes. --> Viable cells were enumerated by trypan blue exclusion using either a C-Chip disposable haemocytometer or a Countess II FL automated cell counter (Thermo Fisher Scientific), depending on the experiment.

Where PBMCs were not required for immediate downstream use, excess cells were cryopreserved in freezing medium consisting of 80% FCS and 20% dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO), aliquoted into cryovials, and transferred to a Mr. Frosty™ controlled-rate freezing container (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at −80 °C overnight before long-term storage in liquid nitrogen.

## 6.3. Neutrophil Isolation from Whole Blood

Neutrophils were isolated from EDTA-anticoagulated peripheral blood using the MACSxpress Whole Blood Neutrophil Isolation Kit (Miltenyi Biotec, Order No. 130-104-434) combined with the MACSxpress Erythrocyte Depletion Kit (Miltenyi Biotec, Order No. 130-098-196), performed with a MACSmix Tube Rotator (Miltenyi Biotec, Order No. 130-090-753) and MACSxpress Separator (Miltenyi Biotec, Order No. 130-098-308). Where required, lyophilised MACSxpress Whole Blood Neutrophil Isolation Cocktail was reconstituted with 2 mL of Neutrophil Isolation Buffer A and the Erythrocyte Depletion Reagent was reconstituted with 2 mL of MACSxpress Erythrocyte Depletion Buffer according to the manufacturer's instructions.

For standard isolation, 1 mL of reconstituted neutrophil isolation cocktail was added to a 15 mL Falcon tube, followed by 1 mL of Neutrophil Isolation Buffer B with three resuspensions. Subsequently, 120 µL of reconstituted Erythrocyte Depletion Reagent was added, followed by 4 mL of EDTA blood (8 mL used in one modified experiment, with an additional erythrocyte lysis step). <!-- TODO: confirm whether the 8 mL blood / additional erythrocyte lysis variant is an intentional protocol modification or a one-off deviation. --> The tube was closed, inverted three times, and incubated for 5 minutes at room temperature on the MACSmix Tube Rotator at 12 rpm. The tube was then placed, without its cap and with the label facing backwards, into the MACSxpress Separator and incubated for 15 minutes at room temperature. The supernatant was carefully transferred to a fresh 15 mL Falcon tube. In the modified variant of this protocol, remaining erythrocytes were further depleted by resuspending the cell pellet in nuclease-free water and centrifuging at 300 × g for 5 minutes prior to resuspension in appropriate medium.

Viable cell concentration was determined using trypan blue exclusion on a C-Chip haemocytometer. For cell counting, 10 µL of cell suspension was mixed with 10 µL of trypan blue; two large squares (first square on the left and fourth square at the bottom) were counted and the cell concentration was calculated as: (cell count in 2 squares ÷ 2) × dilution factor (2) × 10^4^.

## 6.4. Osteoclast Differentiation from Human PBMCs

Osteoclastogenesis was induced in vitro from PBMC-derived monocytes to assess osteoclast differentiation capacity and resorption activity in patients and controls. Following isolation, PBMCs were seeded in adherence medium (α-MEM, 1% PSG, 1% FCS) at a density of 3 × 10^6^ cells/mL into either standard 48-well tissue culture plates (250 µL per well) or calcium phosphate (CAP)-coated 96-well plates (100 µL per well). Plates were incubated for 2 hours at 37 °C with 5% CO~2~ to allow monocyte adherence. Non-adherent cells were removed by aspiration and the adherent monolayer was washed twice with adherence medium.

Osteoclast differentiation was induced by the addition of differentiation medium, consisting of α-MEM supplemented with 10% FCS, 1% PSG, 30 ng/mL macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF), receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL), and, where indicated, transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1). RANKL concentration varied across experimental series: 30 ng/mL was used in early osteoclast experiments (July 2023–April 2024 and February 2025); 10 ng/mL was used in the initial VSIG4/SAPHO osteoclast experiment (15/10/2025) and in later experiments (August–September 2025); and 20 ng/mL was used in the repeat VSIG4/SAPHO experiment (27/10/2025 and 31/10/2025). TGF-β1 (1 ng/mL) was included in the VSIG4/SAPHO osteoclast experiments but was not recorded in early labbook experiments (2023–2024), where only M-CSF and RANKL were documented. <!-- TODO: confirm whether TGF-β1 was used but not recorded in 2023–2024 osteoclast experiments, or genuinely omitted. --> Volumes of 500 µL per well were added to 48-well plates and 200 µL per well to CAP-coated 96-well plates. All cultures were maintained at 37 °C with 5% CO~2~ in a humidified incubator. Medium was replaced every three days with freshly prepared differentiation medium containing identical cytokine concentrations.

Each osteoclast differentiation experiment constituted an independent biological replicate using freshly isolated or thawed PBMCs from individual donors. The number of donors (biological replicates) varied per experiment: early experiments used 1–2 healthy donors; the VSIG4/SAPHO experiments used 1 patient and 2 controls (15/10/2025), or the same samples from cryopreserved stock (repeat, 27/10/2025); and later experiments (August 2025) used 1 patient and 2 controls per run. <!-- TODO: confirm number of technical replicate wells per condition per experiment — plate layouts not consistently recorded. -->

Where inhibition of cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) was required, the selective COX-1 inhibitor SC-560 was added to differentiation medium. SC-560 concentrations and timing of addition varied across experimental series: 20 µg/mL was used in the initial experiment (July 2023); 10 µg/mL in the September and October 2023 experiments; 0.37 µg/mL in the July 2024 experiments; and 0.1, 1, and 2 µM in the February 2025 dose-response experiment. The day of SC-560 addition also varied: day 4 (48-well plates) and day 6 (96-well plates) in February 2025; day 7 in July 2024; and days 6–7 or 8–9 in the July 2024 paired experiment. <!-- TODO: confirm whether the SC-560 concentration/timing variability across experiments reflects intentional dose-finding or a finalised protocol. -->

For morphology and TRAP staining experiments, cultures in 48-well plates were terminated on Day 8. For bone resorption assays, CAP-coated 96-well plate cultures were extended to Day 12. Morphological assessment was performed at Days 3, 6, 7, and 8 by phase-contrast microscopy. Prior to termination, conditioned supernatants (200–400 µL per well) were collected and stored at −80 °C for downstream analysis.

## 6.5. Tartrate-Resistant Acid Phosphatase (TRAP) Staining

TRAP staining was performed on Day 8 of osteoclast culture to confirm osteoclast identity using TRAP Kit 387 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Prior to fixation, 200 µL of conditioned supernatant was removed from each well and stored at −80 °C for downstream analysis; the remaining medium was discarded.

All staining solutions were prepared fresh immediately before use. The fixation solution (total volume 50 mL, prepared under a chemical fume hood) was composed of 12.5 mL citrate solution (supplied in kit), 4 mL of 37% formaldehyde, and 32.5 mL acetone. Components were mixed immediately and used without delay. The TRAP staining solution was prepared in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube by sequential combination and vortexing of the following kit reagents: 3 mL Milli-Q water, 33 µL sodium nitrite, 33.33 µL naphthol, 33 µL fast garnet, 133 µL acetate solution, and 66 µL tartrate solution. The final mixture was vortexed and covered with aluminium foil to protect from light. The staining solution could be stored at 4 °C for up to one week.

Fixation was performed by the addition of 250 µL of fixation solution per well (48-well plate) and incubation for exactly 3 minutes at room temperature. Overfixation was carefully avoided to prevent inactivation of the TRAP enzyme. Wells were washed twice with PBS (Gibco™, pH 7.4). TRAP staining solution (250 µL per well) was then applied and incubated at room temperature with continuous visual monitoring of colour development rather than to a fixed time endpoint; recorded incubation times ranged from 5 to 20 minutes across experiments. Wells were washed once with PBS and 500 µL of glycerin-PBS per well was added for cell preservation. Plates were examined by light microscopy and TRAP-positive multinucleated cells (staining red/purple) were identified as osteoclasts.

## 6.6. Bone Resorption Assay — Silver Nitrate Staining of CAP-Coated Plates

Bone resorption activity was assessed on Day 11–12 of osteoclast culture on calcium phosphate (CAP)-coated 96-well plates by silver nitrate staining to visualise resorption pits. At the end of the culture period, cells were lysed by washing five times with 300 µL of deionised water per well.

Silver nitrate solution (0.5% AgNO~3~) was added to each well and incubated in the dark for approximately one hour. <!-- TODO: confirm silver nitrate volume per well — 100 µL recorded in one entry (VSIG4, Nov 2025) and 200 µL in others; standardise. --> Wells were washed once with 300 µL of deionised water. Development was performed by the addition of sodium carbonate–formalin solution (0.25% Na~2~CO~3~ in 37% formalin) per well, followed by a final wash with 300 µL of deionised water. Plates were then air-dried and resorption pits were visualised and imaged by light microscopy.

## 6.7. Macrophage Differentiation and NLRP3 Inflammasome Stimulation

### 6.7.1. Macrophage Differentiation

PBMC-derived macrophages were generated to assess NLRP3 inflammasome activation in a physiologically relevant primary cell system. This experiment was performed using PBMCs from 2 VSIG4-variant patients and 2 healthy controls (4 biological replicates). Freshly isolated PBMCs were seeded in 12-well tissue culture plates at a density of 1.5 × 10^6^ cells per well in adherence medium (α-MEM, 1% FCS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin) and incubated at 37 °C with 5% CO~2~ for 2 hours. Non-adherent cells were removed and the monolayer was washed. Differentiation was initiated by the addition of macrophage differentiation medium (α-MEM, 10% FCS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 30 ng/mL human M-CSF) and cultures were maintained for 7 days at 37 °C with 5% CO~2~. Medium was replaced every 2–3 days with freshly prepared differentiation medium. Each donor's cells were processed in an independent 12-well plate (one plate per donor). This macrophage-based inflammasome experiment (05/01/2026) is distinct from the earlier direct PBMC stimulation experiments (15/10/2025 and 31/10/2025, @sec-direct-pbmc-stimulation), which used freshly isolated PBMCs plated directly in 48-well plates without a 7-day macrophage differentiation step.

### 6.7.2. NLRP3 Inflammasome Stimulation (Macrophage Experiment) {#sec-nlrp3-macrophage}

On Day 7, macrophages were washed once with warm PBS (Gibco™, pH 7.4) and medium was replaced with fresh α-MEM supplemented with 10% FCS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin, without M-CSF, prior to stimulation. Cells were stimulated according to the following conditions: unstimulated (negative control), DMSO vehicle control (0.1% DMSO), LPS only (1 µg/mL LPS, *Escherichia coli* O111:B4, Sigma-Aldrich; priming for 2 hours), <!-- TODO: confirm 1 µg/mL is the intended LPS working concentration — some lab entries record only "1 µg" without volume context. --> LPS plus nigericin (1 µg/mL LPS for 2 hours followed by 10 µM nigericin, Tocris Bioscience, for 2 hours), and LPS plus nigericin plus MCC950 (1 µg/mL LPS for 2 hours, then MCC950 [10 µM; Merck/Sigma-Aldrich] added simultaneously with 10 µM nigericin). The plate layout shows 3 columns per condition (Rows A–E, Columns 1–3), however the lab notes state "technical replicates: 2 per condition." <!-- TODO: clarify whether 2 or 3 wells per condition were used as technical replicates — plate layout and stated replicate number are inconsistent. --> Nigericin and MCC950 were prepared as 10 mM stocks in DMSO; the final DMSO concentration in all relevant wells was 0.1%.

LPS was prepared as a 1 mg/mL stock in sterile water. Stimulations were conducted sequentially as signal 1 (LPS priming) followed by signal 2 (nigericin, ± MCC950). Conditioned supernatants were collected for IL-1β quantification by ELISA and caspase-1 activity measurement by luminescence assay. Cells were then detached for viable cell counting and normalisation of readouts per 10^5^ cells.

### 6.7.3. Direct PBMC Stimulation {#sec-direct-pbmc-stimulation}

In a separate set of experiments (15/10/2025 and 31/10/2025), freshly isolated PBMCs were stimulated directly without prior macrophage differentiation. PBMCs were plated in 48-well plates at 1 × 10^6^ cells/well in complete medium (α-MEM + 1% PSG + 10% FCS) in a total volume of 500 µL (15/10/2025) or 1 mL (31/10/2025) per well; this volume discrepancy is explicitly recorded in the lab notes. The same stimulation conditions and concentrations described in @sec-nlrp3-macrophage were used. These experiments used 1 SAPHO patient and 2 healthy controls (15/10/2025), with 3 technical replicates per condition. <!-- TODO: confirm number of donors used in the 31/10/2025 repeat. --> The plate layout for the 15/10/2025 experiment included additional wells for unstimulated and stimulated osteoclasts, seeded at 3 × 10^6^ cells/mL for parallel osteoclast differentiation.

## 6.8. RNA Extraction — RNeasy Mini Kit with On-Column DNase Digestion

Total RNA was extracted from neutrophil and osteoclast cell pellets using the RNeasy Mini Kit (Qiagen) with on-column DNase I digestion to remove genomic DNA contamination.

Cell pellets were lysed by the direct addition of 350 µL Buffer RLT, followed by vigorous vortexing or pipetting to ensure thorough lysis. The lysate was transferred to a QIAshredder spin column placed in a 2 mL collection tube and centrifuged at maximum speed for 2 minutes to homogenise the lysate. The homogenised lysate was collected in a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and 350 µL of 70% ethanol was added and mixed thoroughly by pipetting. The mixture (up to 700 µL, including any precipitate) was transferred to an RNeasy spin column in a 2 mL collection tube and centrifuged at ≥8,000 × g (≥10,000 rpm) for 15 seconds; the flow-through was discarded.

On-column DNase digestion was performed by the addition of 80 µL of DNase I incubation mix (10 µL DNase I stock solution combined with 70 µL Buffer RDD from the RNase-Free DNase Set, Qiagen; mixed gently by inversion) directly onto the spin column membrane, and incubated at room temperature (20–30 °C) for 15 minutes. The column was then washed sequentially with 350 µL Buffer RW1 (centrifuged at ≥8,000 × g for 15 seconds), 500 µL Buffer RPE (centrifuged at ≥8,000 × g for 15 seconds), and a second 500 µL of Buffer RPE (centrifuged at ≥8,000 × g for 2 minutes to dry the membrane). All flow-throughs were discarded.

RNA was eluted by transferring the spin column to a new 1.5 mL collection tube, adding 30–50 µL of RNase-free water directly to the membrane, and centrifuging at ≥8,000 × g for 1 minute. Where maximum RNA yield was required, a second elution with a further 30–50 µL of RNase-free water was performed. RNA concentration and purity were assessed spectrophotometrically using a Nanoquant plate reader or Qubit fluorometer, with A260/A280 ratios ≥2.0 considered indicative of adequate RNA purity.

## 6.9. Quantitative Real-Time PCR (qPCR)

Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was performed to assess relative gene expression of *IL1RN* and other targets in neutrophil samples from GPP patients and healthy controls. cDNA was synthesised from isolated total RNA. <!-- TODO: specify reverse transcription kit and reaction conditions — not recorded in lab notes. -->

Four housekeeping genes were used as reference genes for normalisation: *ACTG*, *B2M*, *PGK1*, and *PO*. Separate master mixes were prepared for each TaqMan probe (target and housekeeping genes), each supplemented with a 20% excess volume to account for pipetting losses. Each master mix contained Gene Expression Master Mix, the respective probe/primer set, and nuclease-free water for volume adjustment. <!-- TODO: specify Gene Expression Master Mix volume per reaction — notes refer to a protocol table not reproduced. --> Master mixes were thoroughly vortexed before and immediately prior to pipetting.

Reactions were assembled in a 96-well intermediate plate, with each well containing master mix and 7.5 µL cDNA per well. Wells were mixed thoroughly using an 8-channel pipette by pipetting up and down 40–50 times. Reaction mixtures (15 µL per well) were then transferred in triplicate to a 384-well qPCR plate following the schema of the protocol. The 384-well plate was sealed with adhesive foil and centrifuged at 4,000 rpm for 2 minutes. The plate was loaded into the qPCR instrument and run using the saved template on the analysis computer. <!-- TODO: specify qPCR instrument model and software — not recorded in lab notes. --> Relative gene expression was calculated using the ΔΔCt method, normalising target Ct values against the geometric mean of the four housekeeping genes.

## 6.10. Primer Design

Primers were designed for Sanger sequencing and colony PCR to confirm the identity and orientation of cloned inserts and to verify site-directed mutagenesis of VSIG4 and PTGS1 constructs or CRISPR efficiency. Mutagenic primers for site-directed mutagenesis were designed manually to incorporate the desired missense and stop variants or alternatively designed using the NEBuilder Assembly Tool (New England Biolabs). For all other primers, the tool Primer3web version 4.1.0 was used. Reference sequences were fetched from the UCSC Genome Browser (hg19). In the extended colour options, exons, common SNPs and repeat regions were marked. The annotated sequence was then copied into a Word file, where the positions of the forward and reverse primers were manually located and marked. Primers that overlapped with a SNP or repeat region were excluded and replaced with alternative primer sets. General primer picking conditions were set as follows: primer size minimum 18 bp, optimum 20 bp, maximum 23 bp; primer Tm minimum 57.0 °C, optimum 59.0 °C, maximum 62.0 °C with a maximum Tm difference of 5.0 °C; primer GC content minimum 30.0%, optimum 50.0%, maximum 70.0%. Thermodynamic parameters were calculated using the SantaLucia 1998 table.

## 6.11. Site-Directed Mutagenesis

Site-directed mutagenesis was performed to introduce specific missense and stop variants into wild-type expression vectors (VSIG4 and PTGS1) for functional characterisation. Mutagenesis reactions were performed using AccuPrime Pfx DNA polymerase (Thermo Fisher Scientific) in combination with a SAM-dependent DNA methylase system (@tbl-mutagenesis-reaction).

|:---|---:|
| 10× AccuPrime Pfx Reaction Mix | 5.00 |
| dNTP mix (10 mM each) | 1.00 |
| 10× Enhancer | 5.00 |
| Plasmid DNA template (50 ng/µL) | 1.00 |
| PCR-grade water | 31.60 |
| DNA methylase (4 U/µL) | 1.00 |
| 25× SAM | 2.00 |
| Forward primer (10 µM) | 1.50 |
| Reverse primer (10 µM) | 1.50 |
| AccuPrime Pfx polymerase (2.5 U/µL) | 0.40 |

: Site-directed mutagenesis reaction setup (1× volumes) {#tbl-mutagenesis-reaction}

The forward and reverse mutagenic primers and the AccuPrime Pfx polymerase were added separately from the pre-mixed master mix. The reaction was incubated in a thermocycler using the programme detailed in @tbl-mutagenesis-thermocycler.

| Temperature | Time | Cycles |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 37 °C | 18 min | Preheat |
| 94 °C | 2 min | Initial denaturation |
| 94 °C | 20 sec | |
| 56 °C | 30 sec | 18 cycles |
| 72 °C | 4 min 45 sec | |
| 72 °C | 5 min | Final extension |
| 4 °C | Hold | |

: Mutagenesis thermocycler programme {#tbl-mutagenesis-thermocycler}

Following PCR, a recombination reaction was performed using a recombination kit (Invitrogen). <!-- TODO: confirm exact recombination kit name and catalogue number — described only as "from Invitrogen" in lab notes. --> Components were combined as follows: 4 µL 5× reaction buffer, 10 µL PCR-grade water, 4 µL mutagenesis PCR product, and 2 µL 10× enzyme mix. The reaction was mixed thoroughly and incubated at room temperature for 10 minutes, then terminated by the addition of 1 µL of 0.5 M EDTA.

## 6.12. Transformation of Mutagenesis Products into Chemically Competent E. coli

Chemically competent *Escherichia coli* cells were used to propagate mutagenised and recombined plasmid constructs. One Shot Top10 cells (Invitrogen/Thermo Fisher, Cat. No. C404003 or C404004) were used in the majority of experiments. DH5αT1 cells (Invitrogen/Thermo Fisher, Cat. No. C404003) were used specifically when prior Top10 transformations had failed (05.03.2025, for PTGS1 constructs). <!-- TODO: confirm which competent cell strain was used for VSIG4 constructs. --> One vial of competent cells was thawed on ice per construct. Two microlitres of the recombination reaction was added to the cells and mixed by snapping the bottom of the tube. The mixture was incubated on ice for 12–30 minutes (30 minutes for Top10; 12 minutes for DH5αT1 as recorded).

Heat shock was performed for 30 seconds at 42 °C using a thermomixer. Cells were immediately returned to ice for 2 minutes. SOC medium (250 µL, pre-warmed to room temperature) was added and the suspension was incubated at 37 °C at 225 rpm for 1 hour. The transformed cells were plated on LB agar plates containing the appropriate selection antibiotic (ampicillin or kanamycin as applicable) at volumes of 25, 50, and/or 100 µL per plate. Plates were incubated overnight at 37 °C.

## 6.13. Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) and Colony Screening

Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed to amplify DNA fragments for colony screening and sequence verification. A standard reaction was used, if not indicated otherwise (@tbl-pcr-reaction).

|:---|---:|
| Nuclease-free water | 6.50 |
| Betaine | 3.00 |
| 10× reaction buffer | 1.50 |
| dNTPs | 1.00 |
| DMSO | 0.75 |
| Forward primer (10 µM) | 0.50 |
| Reverse primer (10 µM) | 0.50 |
| MgCl~2~ | 0.45 |
| Taq polymerase | 0.07 |

: PCR reaction setup (1× volumes) {#tbl-pcr-reaction}

Incubation took place in a thermocycler using the programme Cx32 (@tbl-cx32).

| Temperature | Time | Cycles |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 94 °C | 3 min | Initial denaturation |
| 94 °C | 20 sec | |
| 65 °C → 56 °C (−1 °C/cycle) | 60 sec | 9 touchdown cycles |
| 68 °C | 60 sec | |
| 94 °C | 20 sec | |
| 55 °C | 60 sec | 29 amplification cycles |
| 68 °C | 60 sec | |
| 68 °C | 10 min | Final extension |
| 15 °C | Hold | |

: Thermocycler programme Cx32 {#tbl-cx32}

For longer fragments (>1 kbp), the elongation time was adjusted to 1 min per 1 kbp. In some experiments, the programme Cx32_55_2min was used, which employed an annealing temperature of 55 °C and an extension time of 2 minutes. All primers were purchased from Thermo Fisher Scientific. Stock solutions (100 µM) were prepared by dissolving oligonucleotides in nuclease-free water, and working solutions were prepared at a concentration of 10 µM.

Individual bacterial colonies were screened by colony PCR, using the same reaction setup and thermocycler programmes described above, to identify transformants carrying the correct insert. Sterile pipette tips were first dipped into 15 µL of PCR master mix and then placed into 2–3 mL of LB medium supplemented with the appropriate selection antibiotic (ampicillin or kanamycin); these mini-cultures were incubated at 37 °C at 150–200 rpm for 2–3 hours while the colony PCR was run. Colony PCR products were analysed by agarose gel electrophoresis (Section 6.14) to confirm the expected fragment size. Colonies giving a band of the correct size were selected for overnight subculture in 100 mL LB medium (inoculated from 0.5–2 mL of the 2–3 hour mini-culture) at 200 rpm, 37 °C, for plasmid DNA preparation (Section 6.15).

## 6.14. Agarose Gel Electrophoresis

To verify whether PCR fragments had the expected size, agarose gel electrophoresis was performed. Agarose gels of 1–1.5% (w/v) were prepared in TBE buffer. A DNA binding dye was added to the molten agarose before casting. Before loading, 3 µL of loading dye was added to 3–6 µL of PCR product. A 1 kb Plus DNA Ladder (Bio-Rad or NEB) was used as a size reference. Gels were run in TBE-filled electrophoresis chambers at 100–220 V for 20–30 minutes and imaged on a ChemiDoc™ Touch Imaging System (Bio-Rad).

## 6.15. Plasmid DNA Purification — Midiprep (NucleoBond® Xtra Midi)

Large-scale plasmid DNA was purified from 100 mL overnight bacterial cultures using the NucleoBond® Xtra Midi kit (Macherey-Nagel) according to the manufacturer's instructions. The overnight culture was transferred into two 50 mL Falcon tubes and centrifuged at 5,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4 °C. The bacterial pellets were resuspended in 8 mL Buffer RES supplemented with RNase A by vortexing. Buffer LYS (8 mL) was added and the suspension was mixed by gentle inversion (not vortexing) and incubated for 5 minutes at room temperature. The NucleoBond Xtra Column was placed in the column holder with a collection tablet beneath, and 12 mL Buffer EQU was applied to equilibrate the column filter. Buffer NEU (8 mL) was added to the lysate by gentle inversion and the neutralised suspension was loaded onto the column and allowed to flow through by gravity.

An additional 5 mL of Buffer EQU was applied to the filter edge and allowed to flow through completely. The filter was removed and discarded. The column was washed with 8 mL Buffer WASH. A new 50 mL Falcon tube was placed below the column and 3.5 mL of isopropanol was added to the tube before 5 mL Buffer ELU was applied to the column and the eluate collected. The isopropanol–eluate mixture was distributed into 4–5 × 2 mL Eppendorf tubes and centrifuged at maximum speed for 15 minutes. The supernatant was carefully removed. The DNA pellet was washed with 2 mL of 70% ethanol at room temperature and centrifuged at maximum speed for 5 minutes. The ethanol was thoroughly removed and the pellet was air-dried for approximately 30 minutes. The dried pellet was dissolved in 100 µL TE buffer and pooled if multiple tubes were used. DNA concentration and purity (A260/A280) were measured using a Nanoquant plate reader. Typical yields were 900–1,200 ng/µL at A260/A280 ratios of approximately 1.7–1.85.

## 6.16. Sanger Sequencing

Sanger sequencing was performed to confirm the identity and sequence integrity of plasmid constructs following colony PCR and midiprep, and to verify site-directed mutagenesis. PCR products intended for sequencing were first cleaned up using AMPure XP magnetic beads (Beckman Coulter), either manually or via a Biomek pipetting robot. Alternatively, plasmid DNA (50 ng/µL) was used directly in the sequencing reaction without prior cleanup. The sequencing reaction was performed using the BigDye Terminator v3.1 cycle sequencing kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, @tbl-seq-reaction).

| Reagent | Volume (µL) |
|:---|---:|
| Sequencing buffer | 2.00 |
| BigDye Premix | 0.25 |
| Nuclease-free water | 6.00 |
| Forward or reverse primer (10 µM) | 0.30 |
| Cleaned PCR product | 1.00 |
| — or plasmid DNA (50 ng/µL) | 0.66 |

: Sequencing reaction setup (1× volumes) {#tbl-seq-reaction}

The reaction was performed using the thermocycler programme BigDye_55_2min (@tbl-bigdye55). For longer transcripts (>750 bp), the extension step at 60 °C was prolonged to 4 minutes. The total run time was approximately 1 hour 46 minutes.

| Temperature | Time | Cycles |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 96 °C | 10 sec | |
| 55 °C | 10 sec | 25 cycles |
| 60 °C | 2 min | |
| 15 °C | 10 min | Hold |

: Thermocycler programme BigDye_55_2min {#tbl-bigdye55}

The sequencing product was purified using CleanSEQ magnetic beads (Beckman Coulter), either manually on a Kisker magnetic plate or via the Biomek pipetting robot. For manual cleanup, 10 µL of CleanSEQ solution was added to each sequencing reaction, followed by 42 µL of 85% ethanol. The mixture was pipetted up and down seven times and incubated for 3 minutes on the magnetic plate. The supernatant was removed by careful aspiration. Wells were washed with 100 µL of 85% ethanol, incubated for at least 30 seconds, and aspirated. The plate was air-dried for approximately 10 minutes at room temperature. The beads were re-hydrated with 60 µL of nuclease-free water and incubated for 3–5 minutes. The plate was returned to the magnetic plate for approximately 3 minutes, and 40 µL of clear eluate was transferred to a fresh capillary electrophoresis plate. Sequence detection was performed on an ABI 3730 DNA Analyzer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

## 6.17. Transient Transfection of HEK293T Cells

HEK293T cells were maintained in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% L-glutamine, and 1% penicillin/streptomycin in T75 flasks at 37 °C with 5% CO~2~. Cells were subcultured until the required passage. <!-- TODO: confirm passage range used across experiments — passage 6 and passage 8 explicitly recorded; passage 9 not confirmed in lab notes. --> Prior to transfection, cells were harvested using 3–10 mL trypsin per flask (incubated 5–6 minutes), pooled, centrifuged at 300–400 × g for 5 minutes, and resuspended in complete DMEM. Cells were counted on a Countess II FL automated cell counter (Thermo Fisher Scientific) or C-Chip haemocytometer and seeded into 6-well plates at 2–4 × 10^5^ cells/mL in 2 mL per well, approximately 15–22 hours before transfection, to achieve 60–80% confluency at the time of transfection. Each condition (variant construct) was transfected in 3 technical replicates (3 wells per condition per experiment). Multiple independent transfection experiments were performed (29.01.2025, 02.10.2025, 29.12.2025, 19.08.2025, 10.09.2025), each constituting a biological replicate of the transfection assay.

Transfection was performed using jetPRIME transfection reagent (Polyplus Transfection) according to the manufacturer's protocol for 6-well plates. A total of 2 µg DNA per well was used, co-transfected with either an orange fluorescent protein (OFP) or pEGFP-N1 reporter vector in a 9:1 ratio (1.8 µg expression construct : 0.2 µg reporter vector) to allow monitoring of transfection efficiency. For each condition, the required volume of expression construct DNA and reporter vector DNA were combined and added to 200 µL jetPRIME buffer, followed by the addition of 4 µL jetPRIME reagent. Mixtures were vortexed for 1 second, spun down briefly, and incubated for 10 minutes at room temperature before dropwise addition to cells in serum-containing medium.

After approximately 4 hours, the medium was replaced with 2 mL of fresh complete DMEM. Supernatants (200 µL) were collected at 24 or 48 hours post-transfection depending on the experiment (the 30.01.2025 entry records collection at 24 hours; the 31.01.2025 entry records collection at 48 hours with concurrent cell counting and RNA extraction; the 04.10.2025 experiment collected supernatant at 48 hours only), centrifuged at 300 × g for 8 minutes, and the clarified supernatant was stored at −80 °C for downstream ELISA. Cells were harvested by trypsinisation (500 µL trypsin-EDTA per well, 5–10 minutes) for cell counting and RNA extraction. Cell counting was performed in 2 technical replicates per condition using the Countess II FL automated cell counter (10 µL cell suspension mixed with 10 µL trypan blue, both sides of the haemocytometer measured). Transfection efficiency was determined by fluorescence cell counting under bright-field and fluorescent microscopy using a C-CHIP haemocytometer, calculated as: transfection efficiency (%) = (fluorescent cells / total cells) × 100. Fluorescence was also quantified using a Varioskan LUX microplate reader (excitation 530 nm, emission 565 nm for OFP).

## 6.18. Quantification of Prostaglandin E~2~ (PGE~2~) by Competitive ELISA

Prostaglandin E~2~ (PGE~2~) concentrations in cell culture supernatants were quantified using the Cayman Chemical Prostaglandin E Express ELISA Kit (Cat. No. 500141), a competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay employing an acetylcholinesterase (AChE) tracer system.

ELISA buffer (1×) was prepared by diluting one vial of 10× ELISA Buffer Concentrate (Item No. 400060) with 90 mL of ultrapure water, ensuring complete dissolution of any precipitated salts. Wash buffer (1×) was prepared by adding 250 µL of 400× concentrate to 99.75 mL of ultrapure water. The PGE~2~ ELISA Standard (Item No. 414014) was reconstituted in 1.0 mL ELISA buffer to a bulk concentration of 10 ng/mL and stored at 4 °C (stable for up to 4 weeks). Working standards were prepared in eight Eppendorf tubes numbered 1–8: 900 µL of the same conditioned culture medium used in the experiment was added to tube 1 and 500 µL of medium to tubes 2–8. Then 100 µL of bulk standard was added to tube 1 (concentration 1,000 pg/mL) and serially diluted by transferring 500 µL from each tube to the next with thorough mixing. Cell culture supernatants were diluted 1:2 in ELISA buffer (30 µL sample + 30 µL buffer, vortexed) immediately before use, with a second 1:4 dilution prepared where required; samples were kept on ice.

The assay was performed in a competitive format on a pre-coated 96-well plate using 50 µL of diluted sample or standard per well. In the PTGS1 transfection experiment (10.02.2025), samples were assayed in triplicate at two dilutions (1:2 and 1:4) to ensure values fell within the dynamic range and to assess dilution linearity; in other ELISA runs, samples were assayed in duplicate. <!-- TODO: confirm replicate format (duplicate vs. triplicate) per assay date — inconsistent across experiments. --> Fifty microlitres of PGE~2~ AChE tracer was added to all wells except total activity (TA) and blank (Blk) wells, and 50 µL of PGE~2~ monoclonal antibody was added to all wells except TA, non-specific binding (NSB), and Blk wells. The plate was sealed with adhesive film and incubated for 18 hours at 4 °C, as per kit protocol. <!-- TODO: confirm whether a 60-minute room-temperature incubation was used in any experiment, or whether all experiments used the 18 h/4 °C protocol. --> The plate was washed five times with 1× wash buffer. Ellman's Reagent (200 µL per well) was then added and the plate was developed in the dark at room temperature for 60–90 minutes. Absorbance was read at 405 nm (with 415 nm and 420 nm as reference wavelengths, which yielded equivalent readings). Data acquisition was initiated once the B~0~ wells reached an absorbance of ≥0.3 A.U.

A standard curve was fitted using four-parameter logistic (4PL) regression of %B/B~0~ against the log-transformed PGE~2~ concentration. Sample concentrations were corrected for the dilution factor and, where applicable, normalised to viable cell number per well and expressed as pg/cell.

## 6.19. Quantification of IL-1β by ELISA

Interleukin-1β (IL-1β) was quantified in cell culture supernatants using the LEGEND MAX™ Human IL-1β ELISA Kit (BioLegend) according to the manufacturer's protocol for cell culture supernatant samples.

Supernatants were collected from cell cultures into clean tubes and clarified by brief centrifugation if necessary. Aliquots were stored at −70 °C, avoiding repeated freeze-thaw cycles. 20× Wash Buffer was diluted 1:20 with deionised water to prepare 1× Wash Buffer. The lyophilised Human IL-1β Standard was reconstituted with Assay Buffer D as per the Certificate of Analysis and serially diluted to generate an 8-point standard curve with concentrations of 125, 62.5, 31.3, 15.6, 7.8, 3.9, and 2 pg/mL, with Assay Buffer D used as the 0 pg/mL blank. Samples were run undiluted unless the signal was anticipated to exceed the upper limit of quantification, in which case they were diluted in Assay Buffer D.

The pre-coated 96-well strip plate was washed four times with ≥300 µL of 1× Wash Buffer. Fifty microlitres of Assay Buffer D was added to all wells, followed by 50 µL of standards or samples, and the plate was incubated for 2 hours at room temperature on a plate shaker at approximately 200 rpm. The plate was washed four times, and 100 µL of Detection Antibody was added to all wells and incubated for 1 hour at room temperature on a shaker. After a further four washes, 100 µL of Streptavidin-Polymer HRP was added and incubated for 30 minutes at room temperature on a shaker. The plate was washed five times (30–60 seconds soak per wash), and 100 µL of TMB Substrate was added and incubated for 20 minutes in the dark. One hundred microlitres of Stop Solution was added and absorbance was read at 450 nm within 30 minutes (with optional subtraction of the 570 nm reference wavelength). The standard curve was generated using a 4PL or 5PL fit, and sample concentrations were interpolated and corrected for any dilution factor applied.

## 6.20. Caspase-1 Activity Assay — CaspaseGlo® 1 Inflammasome Assay

Caspase-1 activity in cell culture supernatants was measured using the CaspaseGlo® 1 Inflammasome Assay (Promega) to assess NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Released (secreted) caspase-1 was quantified from PBMC supernatants using the supernatant-only protocol (Section 4.B of the kit manual). This assay was performed on supernatants from the PBMC stimulation experiment (15/10/2025), using 2 patients and 2 controls (4 biological replicates), with 3 technical replicates per condition per donor.

CaspaseGlo® 1 Buffer and ZWEHD substrate were brought to room temperature. The substrate was reconstituted in the buffer to generate the base reagent. MG132 (as supplied) was added to generate the CaspaseGlo® 1 No Inhibitor Reagent. The reagent was split equally and Ac-YVAD-CHO was added to one half at a final concentration of 1 µM to generate the CaspaseGlo® 1 + YVAD Reagent. Both reagents were protected from light and maintained at room temperature until use.

Each supernatant sample was tested on two paired 96-well white opaque plates: Plate A (No Inhibitor) and Plate B (+YVAD). Fifty microlitres of PBMC supernatant per replicate was dispensed into corresponding wells on both plates, followed by 50 µL of the respective CaspaseGlo® 1 reagent (No Inhibitor or +YVAD; 1:1 ratio, 100 µL total volume per well). Plates were gently mixed for 30 seconds, covered to avoid evaporation, and incubated at room temperature for at least 60 minutes (stable for 1–3 hours). <!-- TODO: report exact incubation time used per experiment — lab notes state "≥60 min, stable 1–3 h" without a fixed endpoint. --> Luminescence was read on a compatible luminescence plate reader.

Mean blank luminescence was subtracted from all wells. For each donor and condition, the mean of the three replicates was calculated per plate. Caspase-1 specific signal was computed as: No Inhibitor mean − (+YVAD mean). Results were normalised to the unstimulated condition for fold-change analysis.

## 6.21. Bulk RNA-Sequencing Analysis

Differential gene expression analysis was performed on bulk RNA-sequencing data from lesional skin, non-lesional skin, and healthy limb skin samples from GPP patients and controls, using raw count matrices provided by external collaborators (Boehringer Ingelheim). <!-- TODO: describe RNA-seq library preparation method (kit and sequencing platform) or confirm that library prep and sequencing were performed entirely externally. --> Sequence alignment for AGEP samples was performed by a collaborator using the STAR aligner and counting was performed with featureCounts.

Count matrices were imported into R and processed using the DESeq2 package. GPP and healthy control count matrices were integrated by appending healthy control columns to the GPP matrix for joint differential expression analysis. Data quality was assessed using variance stabilising transformation (vst) followed by principal component analysis (PCA) to visualise sample clustering, identify outliers, and assess batch effects and covariates; samples identified as outliers by PCA were excluded from downstream analysis. A DESeq2 dataset object was constructed from the integrated count matrix and sample metadata. Genes with fewer than 10 total counts across all samples were excluded. Differential expression was determined using the DESeq function, with specific contrasts extracted using the results function. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were defined by a log~2~ fold change of ≥1.5 or ≤−1.5 and an adjusted p-value of <0.05 (Benjamini-Hochberg correction). Gene identifiers were annotated by conversion of Ensembl IDs to gene names and symbols.

Results were visualised using heatmaps, volcano plots, MA plots, and scree plots. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and pathway analysis were performed using the clusterProfiler package in R and the web-based Metascape tool. The top 20 enriched pathways and gene sets were prioritised for subsequent variant analysis. Overlapping genes between related pathways were identified using an online Venn diagram tool (Bioinformatics & Evolutionary Genomics). Identified gene sets were used as input for variant prioritisation in the NGS variant analyser. All scripts and output files were stored in `V:\Hueffmeier_GPP\Skin_RNA_analysis_Boeringer.R`, with package versions documented in a `version_info.txt` file for reproducibility.
